title: An outbreak in southern Sudan

title: A second outbreak, a new virus
country: Present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo
summary: A separate investigation in the Yambuku area linked many infections to unsafe injections and close contact. The virus later took its name from the nearby Ebola River. This stop distinguishes the Zaire investigation from the Sudan investigation.

title: Outbreaks recur in Central Africa

title: Kikwit changes the response
summary: The Kikwit outbreak brought renewed attention to surveillance, infection prevention, contact tracing, and community trust. The 2026 anniversary lectures look back on this response, but the outbreak year is 1995, as documented in the original study.

title: Uganda builds a local response
summary: Uganda's 2000–2001 outbreak illustrates the importance of local surveillance, clinical organization, and community structures. It belongs to the Sudan virus lineage, distinct from Ebola virus disease caused by Ebola virus.

source: Lamunu et al., International Journal of Infectious Diseases, 2004

title: A third major Ebola disease virus
summary: Investigation in western Uganda identified Bundibugyo virus as a distinct cause of Ebola disease. Its identification is important for the timeline: outbreaks caused by different viruses cannot be treated as one uniform biomedical event.

source: Wamala et al., Emerging Infectious Diseases, 2010

title: An epidemic crosses borders
summary: The largest Ebola epidemic to date began in southeastern Guinea and spread through the region. At this scale, dated district maps and changing case reports explain more than a single country marker. This 2014 stop represents one stage of a multi-year epidemic.
